parts:
Hi Robson,

It looks like you have all the components from mirt required to compute these indices, and just need to apply a user-defined function to each row in the coef(fit1.irt, simplify = TRUE, IRTpars = TRUE)$items matrix. So something like

myfun <- function(cfs){
  a <- cfs[1]
  b <- cfs[-1]
  .....
  # compute transfomation
}

cfs <- coef(fit1.irt, simplify = TRUE, IRTpars = TRUE)$items
apply(cfs, 1, myfun)

will do the trick. Cheers.

Phil

Em sexta-feira, 17 de fevereiro de 2017 12:28:22 UTC-2, Phil Chalmers escreveu:
Hi Robson,

It looks like you have all the components from mirt required to compute these indices, and just need to apply a user-defined function to each row in the coef(fit1.irt, simplify = TRUE, IRTpars = TRUE)$items matrix. So something like

myfun <- function(cfs){
  a <- cfs[1]
  b <- cfs[-1]
  .....
  # compute transfomation
}

cfs <- coef(fit1.irt, simplify = TRUE, IRTpars = TRUE)$items
apply(cfs, 1, myfun)

will do the trick. Cheers.

Phil
